analysis_steps.goal: Create homogeneous continuum-free CO(3-2) data cubes and MFS continuum maps

method.value: Extract calibrated target visibilities with CASA SPLIT and combine multi-execution MSs with CONCAT. Subtract a 1st-order continuum model fitted to line-free channels (outside +/- 800 km/s of z_CO) using UVCONTSUB. Image line cubes in tclean ('cube' mode, natural weighting, 0.2'' cell size, ~7.812 MHz channels) to make dirty cubes, trim to the CO sideband excluding SPW edge channels with IMSUBIMAGE, compute channel RMS via sigma-clipping, and re-run tclean cleaning down to 3x dirty RMS. Image continuum for 24 non-companion sources using tclean in 'MFS' mode on line-free channels down to 3x RMS.

evidence.quote: We then use the CASA task UVCONTSUB to fit the source visibilities with a first order model using all line-free channels and to subtract this model from the data, resulting in a ‘continuum-free’ MS.
The tclean task is then repeated, but the image is cleaned down to $3\times$ the RMS of the ‘dirty’ image, creating a final ‘clean’ line cube.

For the remaining 24 sources in our sample (see Table [\[basictab\]](#basictab)), we create continuum maps by using the CASA task TCLEAN in ‘MFS’ mode, selecting the line-free channels (see Section [2](#obsdat)).

key_parameters.value: Line-free range: outside +/- 800 km s^-1 of z_CO; cell size = 0.2''; channel width ~7.812 MHz (~25 km s^-1); natural weighting; sigma clipping S/N_upper = 3; clean threshold = 3x dirty RMS

evidence.quote: These continuum-free visibilites are imaged using CASA tclean in ‘cube’ mode with natural weighting and $0.2''$ cells to create a ‘dirty’ line cube. The channel width is kept to its intrinsic value of $\sim7.812$ MHz (roughly 25 km s$^{-1}$).
The RMS noise level of the channel of this cube is calculated using sigma clipping (using astropy SIGMA_CLIPPED_STATS with $S/N_{upper}=3$; (cite: astr13; astr18)).

analysis_steps.goal: 3-D stacking of CO(3-2) cubes, PSF stacking, and moment 0 map creation

method.value: Cut out central 100x100 pixels (20''x20'') of the 7 CO-detected cubes and rebin spectrally onto a -3000 to +3000 km s^-1 grid (240 channels of 25 km s^-1) by fractional velocity bin overlap (Eqs. 1-2) using four weighting schemes (InvV, Norm, InNo, None). Stack median channel synthesized beams in 2-D with identical weights (Eq. 3) and fit a 2-D Gaussian to define the effective PSF. Collapse the 4 stacked cubes over 5 velocity ranges (+/-100 x [1,2,3,4,5] km s^-1) using CASA immoments to create 20 moment 0 maps.

evidence.quote: To begin, we initialize an empty cube with spatial dimensions of 100$\times$100 pixels ($20''\times20''$, with $0.2''$/pixel) and a spectral axis that covers from -3000$<$v$<$3000 km s$^{-1}$ in 240 channels of width 25 km s$^{-1}$.
This stacked PSF is then fit with a 2-D Gaussian, and the best-fit major axis, minor axis, and position angle are set as the PSF (i.e., synthesized beam) for each channel of the stacked cube.

We use each of the four weighting schemes to create a separate stacked cube (CASA immoments). These cubes are then collapsed over five velocity ranges ($\pm100\times[1,2,3,4,5]$ km s$^{-1}$), resulting in 20 moment zero maps (see left panels of Figure [1](#bigbig)).

key_parameters.value: Grid: 100x100 pixels (20''x20'', 0.2''/pixel), 240 channels (-3000 to 3000 km s^-1, width 25 km s^-1); z_stack = 2.337; collapse velocity ranges: +/-100, +/-200, +/-300, +/-400, +/-500 km s^-1

evidence.quote: The redshift of the stacked cube is set to be the average of the input galaxy redshifts (i.e., $z_{stack}=2.337$).

evidence.quote: In each case we assume that the galaxy is centred at the phase centre, which was selected based on rest-frame UV data.
Since the difference in rest-frame UV and CO(3-2) positions are $<1$ px for all sources, this has minimal effect on our analyses.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract radial surface brightness profiles and evaluate deviation from PSF

method.value: Fit a 2-D Gaussian to find the brightness-weighted center of each moment 0 / stacked map, then compute mean surface brightness in circular annuli of width 1 pixel out to r_max (the bin before the first negative-intensity bin). Assign uncertainty in each bin as the maximum of the bin standard deviation and a simulated beam-dependent RMS level. Normalize profile and uncertainty by peak mean value and calculate chi^2 against the normalized PSF radial profile (Eq. 4).

evidence.quote: We begin by finding the brightness-weighted spatial center by fitting a 2-D Gaussian to this emission. We then examine the emission in circular bins of width 1 pixel centered on this spatial position.

In order to determine the uncertainty on the mean in a bin, we take the maximum value of two values: the standard deviation in the bin and a beam-dependent RMS noise level (see Appendix [7](#uncanpp) for full details).
To determine this $\mathrm{r_{max}}$, we determine the smallest bin that features a negative intensity (i.e., $r_n$), and set $\mathrm{r_{max}}$ to the radius of the previous bin (i.e., $r_{n-1}$) .

analysis_steps.goal: Bayesian radial profile fitting with 1-component and 2-component 2-D circular Gaussian models

method.value: Generate 1-component and 2-component 2-D circular Gaussian models, convolve with the representative PSF of the map, extract and normalize the model radial profile to unity at the center, and fit to the observed radial profile using MultiNest / PyMultiNest. Compare models using chi^2, reduced chi^2, and Bayes factor K = Z_1 / Z_2.

evidence.quote: To begin, we create a 2-D circular Gaussian model with arbitrary amplitude and set width (HWHM$_{\mathrm{G1}}$). This model is convolved with the representative PSF of a moment 0 map, and a radial profile of the convolved image is extracted.

By using the Bayesian inference code MultiNest ((cite: fero09)) and its python wrapper (PyMultiNest; (cite: buch14)), we find the best-fit intrinsic FWHM of the model so that the difference between the radial profiles is minimized.

key_parameters.value: 1-Gaussian prior: log10(HWHM_G1/['']) uniform in [-2, 0.5]; 2-Gaussian priors: log10(HWHM_G1/['']) uniform in [-2, 0], log10(HWHM_G2/['']) uniform in [0, 0.5], log10(f_12) uniform in [-3.5, 0)

evidence.quote: We wish to explore a range of intrinsic widths, so we fit for log$_{10}($HWHM$_{\mathrm{G1}})$ (where the HWHM is in units of arcseconds) and set the prior to a uniform distribution between \[-2,0.5\], corresponding to angular scales \[$0.01'',\sim3''$\].

The prior distributions for the two log$_{10}$(HWHM) variables are set to uniform distributions: \[-2,0\] (or \[$0.01'',1''$\]) for log$_{10}($HWHM$_{\mathrm{G1}})$ and \[0,0.5\] (or \[$1'',\sim3''$\]) for log$_{10}($HWHM$_{\mathrm{G2}})$. We adopt a uniform distribution between \[-3.5,0) for $\mathrm{log_{10}(f_{12})}$.

assumptions.value: Circular 2-D Gaussian intrinsic source morphology; neither model preferred a priori in Bayes factor

evidence.quote: While it would be possible to assume a general elliptical Gaussian (or 2-D Sérsic profile; (cite: sers63)) and determine the intrinsic axis ratio and intrinsic position angle of the moment 0 map, we simply wish to search for the existence of diffuse emission, and thus proceed with a simpler 2-D circular Gaussian model.

When considering two models, we may use their relative Bayesian evidences to calculate the Bayes factor: $$\begin{equation} K=\frac{Z_1}{Z_2} \end{equation}$$ where we assume that neither model is preferred *a priori*.

analysis_steps.goal: Order-of-magnitude molecular gas mass estimation for host and extended CGM reservoir

method.value: Estimate host molecular gas mass from representative L'_CO(3-2), r_31, and alpha_CO, and estimate extended CGM molecular gas mass from the ratio of integrated flux densities derived from the 2-Gaussian fit parameters and Milky Way-like r_31 and alpha_CO.

evidence.quote: As a very basic estimate of the host galaxy gas mass, we may consider a representative L’$_{CO(3-2)}\sim10^{10}$ K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$ (cite: circ21), $r_{31}\sim0.97$ (cite: cariw13), and $\alpha_{CO}\sim0.8\,$M$_{\odot}\,$K$^{-1}\,$km$^{-1}\,$s$\,$pc$^{-2}$ (appropriate for high-*z* QSO host galaxies; (cite: deca22)).

Taking the best-fit FWHMs and relative peak intensity from Table [\[pmntable\]](#pmntable), we find that the integrated flux density (S$\Delta v_{CO}$) of the extended component is $\sim2\times$ that of the host galaxy. Using the Milky Way-like values of $r_{31}=0.27$ ((cite: cariw13)) and $\alpha_{CO}\sim4.3$ ((cite: bola13)), we find log$_{10}(M_{H_2,CGM}$/M$_{\odot})\sim10.4$.

key_parameters.value: L'_CO(3-2) ~ 10^10 K km s^-1 pc^2; Host: r_31 ~ 0.97, alpha_CO ~ 0.8 M_sun K^-1 km^-1 s pc^-2; Extended CGM: r_31 = 0.27, alpha_CO ~ 4.3 M_sun K^-1 km^-1 s pc^-2

findings_qualitative.value: A 3-D stack of CO(3-2) emission from seven z ~ 2.0-2.5 AGN host galaxies reveals a compact central component (HWHM ~ 0.8 kpc) surrounded by a weak, spatially extended molecular gas reservoir (HWHM ~ 13.5 kpc, amplitude ~ 0.005 of peak).

evidence.quote: Through a three-dimensional stacking analysis we find evidence for extended CO emission of radius $r\sim13$ kpc.

This best fit model includes a compact, barely resolved source with an amplitude of unity and HWHM=$0.09^{+0.15}_{-0.06}=0.76^{+1.19}_{-0.46}$ kpc, and a more diffuse component with an amplitude of $0.005^{+0.004}_{-0.002}$ and HWHM=$1.66^{+0.58}_{-0.43}"=13.49^{+4.71}_{-3.49}$ kpc.

findings_qualitative.value: Stacked HST/ACS F814W rest-frame UV images show complex small-scale morphology out to r ~ 5-10 kpc for both narrow-line and broad-line AGN, but no extended emission at the r ~ 13 kpc scale of the CO reservoir.

evidence.quote: We extend this analysis to the HST/ACS i-band images of the sample galaxies, finding a complex small-scale ($r<10$ kpc) morphology but no robust evidence for extended emission.

A similar stacking and radial profile analysis is run on HST/ACS i-band SUPER galaxies, finding evidence for complex behaviour for $r\lesssim10$ kpc but no emission at the CO-derived radius of $r\sim13$ kpc. If the sample is split into NL and BL AGN, then this behaviour is present for both subsamples.

findings_qualitative.value: The 2-D stack of rest-frame FIR (~870 um) continuum emission across 24 SUPER sources is unresolved and best fit by a point source (r <= 5 kpc).

evidence.quote: We find that a point source returns the best fit, implying that the emission is unresolved. Using the average redshift of this sample ($z\sim2.3$), this implies an upper limit on the continuum size of $\lesssim0.6''\sim5$ kpc.

findings_qualitative.value: The extended CO(3-2) emission is most likely an enriched molecular gas reservoir populated by past AGN- or starburst-driven outflows rather than discrete satellite galaxies or pristine cosmological filaments.

evidence.loc: How was the extended gaseous reservoir formed?
evidence.quote: In summary, we find it unlikely that the extended emission is caused by a gaseous filament or individual satellite galaxies. The observed outflows feature sufficient velocities to populate an enriched gaseous reservoir at the observed radius.

Based on our analyses of the ALMA CO(3-2) and HST/ACS i-band emission, we conclude that the most likely case is that this emission represents processed material ejected from the host galaxy by past outflows.

claims.hypothesis: Energetic, outflowing z ~ 2.0-2.5 AGN host galaxies from the SUPER sample are surrounded by an extended molecular gas reservoir in their circumgalactic medium.
claims.experiment: Perform 3-D image-plane stacking of homogeneous ALMA CO(3-2) data cubes for 7 AGN host galaxies, collapse over +/-100 km s^-1, extract radial surface brightness profiles, and fit 1- and 2-component 2-D circular Gaussian models convolved with the stacked PSF using PyMultiNest.
claims.result: The 2-Gaussian model is strongly preferred (chi^2 = 0.58 vs 4.14, Bayes factor K ~ 27), yielding a compact core of HWHM = 0.76 (+1.19/-0.46) kpc and an extended component of HWHM = 13.49 (+4.71/-3.49) kpc with relative peak amplitude 0.005 (+0.004/-0.002).
claims.finding: AGN host galaxies at cosmic noon possess an extended, low-surface-brightness molecular gas reservoir on ~13 kpc scales.

evidence.quote: We find that the Two Gaussian model is strongly favored ($K\sim27$).

This best fit model includes a compact, barely resolved source with an amplitude of unity and HWHM=$0.09^{+0.15}_{-0.06}=0.76^{+1.19}_{-0.46}$ kpc, and a more diffuse component with an amplitude of $0.005^{+0.004}_{-0.002}$ and HWHM=$1.66^{+0.58}_{-0.43}"=13.49^{+4.71}_{-3.49}$ kpc.

claims.hypothesis: The extended CO(3-2) emission traces a circumgalactic gas reservoir that is morphologically distinct from the stellar and dust components of the host galaxies.
claims.experiment: Perform 2-D inverse-variance stacking and radial profile analysis on HST/ACS F814W rest-frame UV images (21 sources, plus NL/BL subsets) and ALMA rest-frame ~870 um FIR continuum maps (24 sources).
claims.result: The HST stack shows complex structure within r < 10 kpc and no significant emission beyond ~7.5-10 kpc; the FIR continuum stack is unresolved (best fit by the PSF, r <= 5 kpc).
claims.finding: The r ~ 13 kpc molecular gas reservoir extends well beyond both the young stellar distribution and the dust continuum, indicating a multi-layered structure and a distinct CGM component.

evidence.quote: However, we may state that the stacked HST/ACS i-band data shows no evidence for significant extended emission beyond $\sim7.5$ kpc, unlike the ALMA CO(3-2) data.

We find that a point source returns the best fit, implying that the emission is unresolved. Using the average redshift of this sample ($z\sim2.3$), this implies an upper limit on the continuum size of $\lesssim0.6''\sim5$ kpc.

claims.hypothesis: The extended CO(3-2) reservoir was formed by processed gas ejected via past outflows rather than discrete satellite galaxies, infalling pristine filaments, or inside-out disk growth.
claims.experiment: Compare the HST F814W stack (to test for satellite stellar light), observed [OIII] outflow velocities (~650-2700 km s^-1) and travel timescales (~13 Myr at 1000 km s^-1), and expected low density/metallicity of cosmic filaments.
claims.result: No extended stellar halo is seen in the unconvolved HST stack to support satellites, filaments are too metal-poor/diffuse to emit strongly in CO, and observed outflow velocities can easily reach ~13 kpc within ~13 Myr, though convolving HST with the ALMA beam and inside-out star formation leave some ambiguity.
claims.finding: Past AGN- or starburst-driven outflows are the most likely origin of the extended molecular reservoir, though inside-out growth cannot be completely ruled out without higher-sensitivity observations.

evidence.loc: How was the extended gaseous reservoir formed?
evidence.quote: In summary, we find it unlikely that the extended emission is caused by a gaseous filament or individual satellite galaxies. The observed outflows feature sufficient velocities to populate an enriched gaseous reservoir at the observed radius.
However, we note that other explanations (e.g., inside-out star formation) are also possible, and further data (e.g., high-sensitivity ACA observations) are required for a robust conclusion.

why_this_data.value: SUPER AGN host galaxies at z ~ 2.0-2.5 have well-characterized multiwavelength properties and ubiquitous [OIII] outflows, and were observed in CO(3-2) with ALMA; re-analyzing from raw visibilities ensures homogeneous data cubes for stacking.

evidence.quote: SINFONI observations of the \[O III\]$\lambda$5007 line in 21 of these sources reveal evidence for outflows in every observed source (cite: kakk20), with large outflow velocities ($\sim10^3$ km s$^{-1}$).
Since our science goals require homogeneity of the data, we chose to reanalyze each dataset, beginning at the visibilities.

why_this_method.value: Individual CO(3-2) detections have low S/N (< 5 sigma), requiring 3-D cube stacking to reach the sensitivity needed for faint extended emission; image-plane stacking allows inspection for discrete companions and 2-D circular Gaussian fitting with PSF convolution measures intrinsic deconvolved sizes.

evidence.quote: While each of the sources in our subsample have been detected in CO(3-2) emission, most of them have relatively low significance (i.e., $<5\sigma$ in integrated intensity). Since we wish to search for low-level emission, we require higher S/N, and thus must perform stacking of each data cube.
This is where image-plane stacking is useful, as we may examine the full 2-D distribution of flux and search for discrete emission that may signal a satellite galaxy.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Realigning each CO(3-2) cube to a 2-D Gaussian centroid of its moment 0 map prior to stacking (rejected because low S/N ~ 3-4 of individual sources would skew centroids toward noise peaks, and UV-to-CO offsets are < 1 pixel)

evidence.quote: As an alternative, it is theoretically possible to fit each ALMA CO(3-2) moment zero map with a 2-D Gaussian model, and realign each cube to the resulting spatial centroid. But since multiple sources in this sample feature low integrated CO S/N values ($\sim3-4$), this approach is likely to be skewed by noise peaks.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Stacking CO-undetected sources (rejected because large velocity offsets up to ~1500 km s^-1 between z_spec and z_CO mean the true systemic CO velocity is unknown)

evidence.quote: Note that we do not attempt to stack sources undetected in CO(3-2) emission. This is due to large differences between previously determined $z_{spec}$ values and the redshift of CO emission of SUPER sources (i.e., up to $\sim1500$ km s$^{-1}$, see Table [\[basictab\]](#basictab)).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fitting elliptical 2-D Gaussian or 2-D Sersic models to the stacked CO moment 0 map (rejected in favor of circular 2-D Gaussians because stacking averages out non-axisymmetric features)

evidence.quote: While it would be possible to assume a general elliptical Gaussian (or 2-D Sérsic profile; (cite: sers63)) and determine the intrinsic axis ratio and intrinsic position angle of the moment 0 map, we simply wish to search for the existence of diffuse emission, and thus proceed with a simpler 2-D circular Gaussian model.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Visibility-plane stacking (discussed as an alternative that avoids cleaning and sidelobe issues, deferred to future work)

evidence.quote: While these factors result in a greatly lessened effect of sidelobes in our analysis, we note that the best way to ensure their absence is to switch from the image plane to visibility-based analysis (e.g., (cite: fuji19), Scholtz et al. submitted).

limitations_admitted.value: Molecular gas mass of the extended CGM component cannot be tightly constrained because the CO excitation ratio r_31 and conversion factor alpha_CO are unknown for high-z AGN CGM.

evidence.quote: Because $r_{31}$ and $\alpha_{CO}$ have not been derived for the CGM of AGN host galaxies at cosmic noon, we are not able to place precise constraints on M$_{H_2,CGM}$.

limitations_admitted.value: Convolving the stacked HST image with the coarse ALMA beam produces a radial profile that is also best fit by a two-Gaussian model (r ~ 1 kpc and r ~ 18 kpc), making it ambiguous whether the extended HST profile under convolution is due to resolution effects or discrete foreground/satellite companions at ~1-2''.

evidence.quote: In summary, our test of convolving the HST stacked image to the ALMA resolution reveals a radial brightness distribution is deviates from a single resolved source, but it is not clear if this is due to resolution effects or the presence of foreground galaxies.

limitations_admitted.value: Cleaning down to a 3-sigma threshold in image-plane analysis does not remove PSF sidelobes below 3-sigma, which could affect low-level extended emission.

evidence.quote: Since we use a threshold of $3\sigma$ (see Section [2](#obsdat)), it is possible that we have not fully subtracted the sidelobes of the PSF.

limitations_admitted.value: Reduced chi^2 values are sub-unity due to conservative uncertainty estimates on the radial profile bins, and the low number of radial bins precludes using AIC or BIC.

evidence.quote: We note that the two-component model has a $\chi^2$ value that is sub-unity, which usually indicates overfitting. However, this is likely due to our conservative uncertainty limits (see Appendix [7](#uncanpp)).
Due to the low number of data points, we are not able to use the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) or Akaike Information Criterion (AIC; e.g., (cite: lidd07; conc19)).

referee_caveats_inferred: The extended CO(3-2) signal is only strongly favored by the Bayesian evidence in a single narrow velocity slice (+/-100 km s^-1) under inverse-variance weighting (which allows the brightest sources to dominate), while the 2-D stack of full-linewidth moment 0 maps yields an inconclusive Bayes factor (K ~ 2).

Because image-plane cleaning stops at 3x RMS and the extended component has a peak amplitude of only ~0.5% of the central component, uncleaned PSF sidelobes of the central emission sit entirely below the clean threshold and are not deconvolved.

When the HST F814W stack is convolved with the ~1.3'' ALMA beam, it also prefers a two-Gaussian fit with an outer component of r ~ 18 kpc, raising the caveat that beam-smearing of compact clumpy structure or nearby companions at 1-2'' could mimic an extended halo at ~1.3'' resolution.
